title: Forgetting constant module coefficients compares derived restriction kernels
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in a common universe containing objects, arrows, covering index sets and coefficients [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative unital ring, $A_{\mathcal C}$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $V:\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal C})\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $v:A\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the scalar-forgetting functors [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a monomorphism $m:W\to T$ in $\mathcal C$, set
$$S_m^A(M)=\ker(M(T)\to M(W)),\qquad S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(G)=\ker(G(T)\to G(W)),$$
with restriction as the arrow and the induced maps on kernels as the functorial action. Both functors are additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Use bounded-below derived functors and integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories].

The category $\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal C})$ is abelian and has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. If $I$ is an injective module sheaf [def-sp-injective-resolutions], its restriction $I(T)\to I(W)$ is surjective and $VI$ is $S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}$-acyclic, meaning $R^qS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VI)=0$ for every $q>0$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$c_m(K):vRS_m^A(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}RS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VK)$$
for $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal C}))$, normalized by the identity $vS_m^A=S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}V$ in degree zero.

More precisely, choose any bounded-below complex $L$ of injective module sheaves representing $K$, any bounded-below complex $J$ of injective abelian sheaves representing $VK$, and any quasi-isomorphism $q:VL\to J$ inducing these identifications. The maps
$$\ker(vL(T)\to vL(W))\xrightarrow{\ker(q)}\ker(J(T)\to J(W)),\quad q_T:vL(T)\to J(T),\quad q_W:vL(W)\to J(W)$$
form a morphism between the degreewise short exact restriction-kernel sequences. All three maps are quasi-isomorphisms. On derived objects the first is $c_m(K)$ and the last two are precisely the canonical ordinary evaluation comparisons of [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget]. These identifications are independent of $L,J,q$ and natural in $K$. No injectivity of $VL^r$ in abelian sheaves and no flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective. Agent-formulated supported refinement of the existing ordinary derived evaluation comparison lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget; the source tag supplies module-injective restriction surjectivity, not the whole comparison. Enough injectives: injectives.tex Tag 01DU, theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives.

proof.text: The module category is abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian] and is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], applied to the sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O=A_{\mathcal C}$ on the small site, hence has (functorial) injective embeddings, in particular enough injectives, by [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding]. The abelian sheaf category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Evaluation is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The kernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives the same properties for module evaluation and for $S_m^A,S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}$: a section of a kernel is a section mapped to zero, and restricting it to zero is precisely the same condition in that subsheaf. Forgetting scalars preserves kernels, giving the identity $vS_m^A=S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}V$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] gives exactness of $V$; its sheafification hypothesis holds on the small site in the given universe. The ordinary module-forgetting $v$ preserves kernels and cokernels sectionwise. Thus both induce the functors on derived categories used in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03FD setup; Modules on Sites Tag 03DA; Injectives Tag 01DU

proof.text: For an injective module sheaf $I$, apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-injective-mono-restriction] with $\mathcal O=A_{\mathcal C}$ and the given monomorphism $m$. This gives surjectivity of $I(T)\to I(W)$. Apply the same node with $\mathcal O=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ to an injective abelian sheaf: its unique integer action identifies abelian sheaves and integer-module sheaves, including their morphisms and injectivity. Hence the restriction-kernel row is short exact for either kind of injective sheaf. This uses module injectivity for $I$, without treating $VI$ as abelian-injective.

For any injective module sheaf $I$, [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] applied to $I[0]$ says that $VI$ is acyclic for evaluation at both $T$ and $W$. The general objectwise comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] identifies these groups with module-derived evaluation, which vanishes in positive degrees on $I$. Thus $H^q(T,VI)=H^q(W,VI)=0$ for $q>0$, and in degree zero the identifications are the actual sections and restrictions.

Take an abelian injective representative $J$ of $VI[0]$ concentrated in nonnegative degrees, using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Step 2 applied to its terms gives a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(J)\to J(T)\to J(W)\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] and Step 3 its cohomology sequence starts $0\to S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VI)\to I(T)\to I(W)\to H^1(S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(J))\to0$, and $H^q(S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(J))=0$ for $q\ge2$. Step 2 makes $I(T)\to I(W)$ surjective, so the remaining $H^1$ also vanishes. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies $S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(J)$ with $RS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VI[0])$. Consequently $R^qS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VI)=0$ for every $q>0$. The long exact sequence here is for complexes of abelian groups, not for a sequence of functors.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 093X, 03FD; derived.tex Tags 013K, 05TH

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective module representative $L$ for $K$ and an abelian injective representative $J$ for $VK$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], applied separately to the module and abelian kernel functors, gives $RS_m^A(K)=Q(S_m^A(L))$ and $RS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VK)=Q(S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(J))$ canonically. The underlying complex of $S_m^A(L)$ is $S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VL)$ by Step 1. Thus these two actual kernel complexes represent the two sides to be compared. This invokes the bounded-below injective-complex clause directly.

source.place: Tags 013K and 070J, injective representatives; Tags 05TI and 05TH, computation on bounded-below injective complexes

proof.text: The complex $J$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents the chosen derived identification $QVL\simeq QJ$ by a chain map $q:VL\to J$, necessarily a quasi-isomorphism. For any such $q$, [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] identifies $q_T$ and $q_W$ with the canonical ordinary derived evaluation comparisons, so they are quasi-isomorphisms. Step 2, applied to all terms of $L$ and $J$, gives degreewise short exact restriction-kernel sequences. Naturality of the chain map $q$ gives $q_W\,vL(m)=J(m)q_T$; hence restricting $q_T$ to the kernels defines a chain map and a morphism of these short exact sequences.

source.place: Tags 093X and 03FD; derived.tex Tag 070I, maps into K-injective complexes

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] the two short exact sequences of Step 6 give a commuting ladder of long exact cohomology sequences. For each integer $n$, use the five-term window $H^{n-1}(L(T))\to H^{n-1}(L(W))\to H^n(S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VL))\to H^n(L(T))\to H^n(L(W))$, with scalar forgetting understood, and the corresponding window for $J$. The first, second, fourth and fifth vertical maps are isomorphisms by Step 6. The abelian five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] makes the middle map an isomorphism. Hence the kernel map is a quasi-isomorphism, completing the assertion for all three displayed maps.

source.place: Tag 0117, functorial long exact sequence; Tag 05QB, five lemma

proof.text: Let $\alpha$ be the natural transformation for the abelian kernel functor in clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Apply its naturality to $q:VL\to J$. Its component on $J$ is an isomorphism by clause (2); therefore the kernel map of Step 7, under the identifications of Step 5 and $Qq$, is exactly $\alpha_{VL}:Q(S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VL))\to RS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(QVL)$. This defines $c_m(K)$. Maps between injective module representatives are represented by chain maps, uniquely up to homotopy, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; all the additive functors here preserve homotopies by applying them to $h-h'=ds+sd$. Naturality of $\alpha$ now proves naturality in $K$ and independence of $L$. For fixed $L$, maps into any abelian injective representative inducing the same derived identification are unique up to homotopy by that same node; thus changing $J,q$ leaves the comparison unchanged. The evaluation maps are the canonical comparisons of [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget]. In degree zero the injective resolutions identify $H^0$ with the original left-exact functors, so the kernel map is precisely the identity $vS_m^A=S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}V$.
